outline.title: Introduction
outline.description: Provide a general overview of Large Language Models (LLMs), their growing adoption, and the emerging security concerns. Motivate the need for a systematic survey of threats.

outline.title: Background
outline.description: Define key concepts: LLMs, transformer architecture, fine-tuning, in-context learning, RLHF. Provide the foundational knowledge needed to understand the attacks.

outline.title: Prompt Injection Attacks
outline.description: Describe direct and indirect prompt injection attacks in detail. Cover techniques like goal hijacking, payload splitting, and jailbreaking. Include real-world examples and defenses.

outline.title: Data and Model Poisoning
outline.description: Explain training-time attacks: data poisoning, backdoor attacks, and model poisoning. Cover how malicious data can compromise model behavior and how to detect/mitigate such attacks.

outline.title: Adversarial Attacks
outline.description: Discuss adversarial examples and perturbations applied to LLMs. Cover both white-box and black-box attack strategies, including token-level and semantic-level attacks.

outline.title: Hallucinations and Factual Accuracy
outline.description: Analyze the hallucination problem in LLMs. Discuss causes, types of hallucinations, detection methods, and mitigation strategies.

outline.title: Defenses and Mitigation Strategies
outline.description: Survey the main defensive techniques: input/output filtering, guardrails, red-teaming, alignment techniques, and formal verification approaches.

outline.title: Discussion and Open Challenges
outline.description: Identify gaps in current research, discuss limitations of existing defenses, and highlight promising future research directions.

outline.title: Conclusion
outline.description: Summarise the key findings, contributions of the survey, and practical recommendations for practitioners.
